subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate, and Core1A/Core1B may not consult one.

must_contain: A surface normal at every refracting boundary before angle language is used.
The incident and refracted media named before deciding toward-normal or away-from-normal bending.
A parallel-sided glass-slab example showing two boundary events rather than one memorized kink.

controlled_variation.hold: the same two transparent media and boundary orientation
controlled_variation.notice: the refracted angle changes but both angles remain normal-referenced
the toward/away bending reverses when the speed/index change reverses

controlled_variation.hold: parallel slab faces and incident direction
controlled_variation.notice: the emergent ray remains parallel in the simple model while lateral displacement changes

must_contain: n = c/v interpreted as a speed ratio, not a material score with no physical meaning.
Snell's law written with the medium labels attached to n1 and n2 and angles measured from the normal.
A limiting comparison that higher refractive index means lower light speed in the ordinary transparent-medium model.

controlled_variation.notice: the refraction angle adjusts through n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r)
sin(i)/sin(r) remains fixed for the same model conditions

controlled_variation.vary: the unit system used for c and v
controlled_variation.hold: their ratio represents the same medium
controlled_variation.notice: refractive index stays dimensionless when compatible speed units are used

must_contain: Principal axis, optical centre and both focal points labelled before principal rays are used.
At least two independent valid principal rays locating one common image or backward-extension point.
A convex-lens focal-length practical interpretation using a distant object without making the Sun the required source.

controlled_variation.vary: which valid pair of principal rays is used
controlled_variation.hold: the same object point and thin lens
controlled_variation.notice: every valid pair locates the same image point within the model

controlled_variation.vary: object position for a convex lens
controlled_variation.notice: image position, size and real/virtual character change systematically
converging and diverging ray rules differ but still use one optical centre and paired foci

must_contain: The optical centre, incident-light direction and vertical sign convention declared before u, v and f receive signs.
1/v - 1/u = 1/f used without making derivation a learner requirement.
A ray-diagram image-region prediction compared with the algebraic result.
Thin-lens/paraxial model conditions stated before treating the equation as authoritative.

controlled_variation.vary: object distance within the paraxial thin-lens model
controlled_variation.hold: lens focal length and sign convention
controlled_variation.notice: the equation prediction tracks the ray construction
the signed result changes consistently with converging versus diverging behavior

controlled_variation.vary: ray angle away from the principal axis
controlled_variation.notice: the simple equation is a model whose geometric accuracy is tied to the paraxial approximation

must_contain: m = v/u and m = h_i/h_o connected for the same lens image.
One negative-magnification and one positive-magnification interpretation.
Magnitude separated from sign: |m| controls relative size while sign controls orientation.

controlled_variation.vary: object position for one convex lens
controlled_variation.notice: magnification magnitude and sign follow the same image-state change seen in the ray diagram

controlled_variation.hold: the same object orientation and sign convention
controlled_variation.notice: the magnification sign and magnitude remain physical predictions rather than formula decorations

must_contain: Focal length converted to metres before P = 1/f is evaluated in dioptres.
The focal-length sign retained so converging and diverging lenses have opposite power signs.
At least one conversion in both directions between focal length and power.

controlled_variation.notice: shorter focal length gives larger positive power magnitude
power changes sign while magnitude stays the same

controlled_variation.vary: centimetres versus metres in the stated focal length
controlled_variation.notice: the numerical power is unchanged only after the unit conversion is handled correctly

family.invariant_demand: Translate the optical setup into normal-referenced refraction or a thin-lens ray construction, preserve the declared medium/coordinate semantics, and cross-check signed formula results against the physical ray picture.
family.difficult_move: Keeping the boundary normal, medium order, thin-lens Cartesian signs and paraxial model consistent across diagrams and equations instead of selecting formulas from surface keywords.
family.independent_check: Snell geometry must agree with the index comparison; a valid lens ray construction, signed lens equation and magnification must predict compatible image location/orientation; power must match signed focal length in metres.

support_ladder.handed_over: The boundary normal or lens principal axis/optical centre is drawn, media or focal points are labelled, and the relevant sign directions are declared.
The optical elements and requested quantities are labelled, but the learner chooses the normal/principal rays, signs and relation.
Only the physical optical setup and requested result are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: Convert a glass-slab or lens ray drawing into normal-referenced angles or signed u, v and f values without changing the physical prediction.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which angles/signs follow from the drawn normal, media and incident-light direction

transfer.changed_demand: Use a thick lens or strongly non-paraxial rays and decide whether the Grade-10 thin-lens equation is an adequate model.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the thin-lens/paraxial conditions are satisfied

transfer.changed_demand: Given only a signed power, infer lens type and focal length without a lens sketch.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the focal-length sign and metre conversion implied by the power

transfer.changed_demand: A convex lens produces a real image with known signed u and v; infer magnification and check orientation against an independently drawn ray pair.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the orientation encoded by the sign of m
